correctness.rationale: Complete exact proof: a nonconstant periodic orbit has constant squared radius because the scalar radial ODE cannot be nontrivially periodic; transverse log multiplier equals 2s_i P'(s_i)T_i and angular period equals 2π/Q(s_i). Factoring P=R B forces two B node values. Opposite signs force an extra positive B root. For same-sign values, the unique degree-one interpolant has a positive root precisely outside the stated degree-five/degree-seven regime; the globally positive weighted cardinal-square construction achieves the two circles at degree nine. Bounds on deg P make degrees five/seven/nine sharp. The potentially borderline zero at s=0 is an equilibrium only. Standard-library exact rational verification passed representative cases; finite checks are corroborative, not the proof.

value.rationale: The two-circle inverse synthesis question is the smallest natural multi-cycle stability-design problem. Data with identical target circles, periods and alternating qualitative stability can require different minimum polynomial degrees, quantitatively 5, 7 or 9. The strict global no-other-cycle condition requires sign control on an entire half-line, not simply ordinary pointwise polynomial interpolation; the degree-nine obstruction is a genuine extra periodic circle forced at all lower allowable degrees. Exact classification allows rigorous choice of oscillator complexity for prescribed periods and Floquet decay/growth rates, without pretending relevance to unrestricted planar systems.
